title: Composite Heuristic Suggester and Explainability Strip for Batching + Cache
creator: Riley Morgan
description: Design a lightweight 'heuristic suggester' UI component in the Redwood Console that offers composite recommendations for batching and KV-cache policy. The component must explain trade-offs, show expected token savings and latency impact, and provide safe guardrails + one-click apply.
spec: Goals: 1) Surface contextual suggestions computed by backend optimizer. 2) Explain why a suggestion is good (e.g., high prefix reuse). 3) Offer guardrail sliders (latency tolerance, quality threshold) and simulated impact preview. Interaction patterns: compact card in model route header, expanded modal for policy composition, inline help microcopy. States: empty/no data, low-confidence suggestion, conflict with existing rollouts, applied, rollback. Accessibility: keyboard nav, color contrast, aria-live for simulation results.
user_flows: developer lands on model route and sees suggestor card
clicks 'preview' to open composition modal with scenario toggles
adjusts latency/quality sliders and observes simulation chart update
applies recommendation to a canary rollout or saves as preset
monitor shows estimated cost reduction and SLO impact post-apply
acceptance_criteria: Card surfaces a recommendation for >70% of sampling traces where prefix-match ratio > 0.3
Preview modal shows token-savings and latency curves updated within 300ms for toggles
Applied policy creates a canary rollout entry and emits instrumentation event batchcache.suggester.apply
Guardrail sliders persist in preset and cannot set quality below org baseline
